subject.title: fix(sessions): enforce exact owner equality for all parent session use and narrow catch

question: Should plugin-runtime session operations consistently fail closed on legacy ownerless rows, and which shared gateway helper should own that authorization across create, reset, patch, and delete?
rationale: Ownerless rows have no safely inferable plugin owner, but rejecting them can break existing plugin workflows; the permanent authorization owner and upgrade boundary require explicit maintainer intent rather than separate PR-local policies.

options.title: Unify and fail closed
options.body: Consolidate all session mutations on one exact-owner guard, reject ownerless rows for plugin runtimes, and document and prove the upgrade behavior.

options.title: Add an ownership migration
options.body: Define a trustworthy migration or operator-assisted ownership assignment before enabling strict rejection, then use the same shared guard everywhere.

options.title: Pause the ownership cluster
options.body: Hold this PR and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/103534 until maintainers define a single session authorization model.

recommendation.title: Unify and fail closed
recommendation.body: Consolidate all session mutations on one exact-owner guard, reject ownerless rows for plugin runtimes, and document and prove the upgrade behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: Prior review and the contributor discussion already identify Takhoffman as the best available owner for the ownerless-session and shared-helper decision.
